    10	/-!
    11	# Representability of the widened divisor functor
    12	
    13	The universal widened class on every divisor chart satisfies the classifier clause, hence
    14	represents the positive-genus divisor functor by `DivScheme`.  The window bound follows from
    15	nonzero genus.  In genus zero the widened functor is terminal, so choosing finite bases internally
    16	gives an unconditional representer without adding a hypothesis to the curve data.
    17	-/

    20	set_option quotPrecheck false
    21	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
    22	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 8
    23	set_option maxRecDepth 16000
    24	
    25	universe u
    26	
    27	open CategoryTheory Opposite
    28	
    29	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    30	
    31	open Grassmannian Scheme

    34	  Scheme.functionFieldOverModule

    41	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

    45	    C.left.Over (Spec (.of k)) := ⟨C.hom⟩
    46	
    47	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k))] [IsIntegral C.left]
    48	  [LocallyOfFiniteType (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    49	  [QuasiCompact (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    50	  [Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 0)]
    51	  [Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1)]
    52	variable (hpi : pi ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.left ↘ Spec (.of k))
    53	variable (g : Nat)
    54	variable (hO : Sheaf.h0 (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1)
    55	  (hchi : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (g : Int))
    56	
    57	section Based
    58	
    59	variable (r1 r2 : Nat)
    60	variable (b1 : Module.Basis (Fin r1) k
    61	  ↥(divisorSections k (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤))
    62	variable (b2 : Module.Basis (Fin r2) k
    63	  ↥(divisorSections k
    64	    ((windowM_choice pi hpi g + windowS_choice pi hpi g) • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤))
    65	
    66	local notation "DivOver" =>
    67	  divSchemeOver k (windowS_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi)
    68	    (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) g r1 r2 b1
    69	    (b2.map (windowShiftEquiv hpi g).symm)
    70	
    71	include hO hchi in
    72	/-- For nonzero genus, the universal widened chart classes represent the divisor functor by
    73	the existing divisor scheme. -/
    74	noncomputable def divFunctorAff_representableBy_divScheme_of_ne_zero (hg : g ≠ 0) :
    75	    (divFunctorAff C g).RepresentableBy DivOver := by
    76	  let hb := windowBound_pos_of_genus_ne_zero pi hpi g hg hO hchi
    77	  exact divFunctorAff_representableBy_of_chartClause hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2
    78	    (fun i j => PointwiseAchiever.divFamZarAffUniv C hpi g r1 r2 b1
    79	      (b2.map (windowShiftEquiv hpi g).symm) i j hO hchi hb)
    80	    (fun i j => PointwiseAchiever.isDivRepClassifyAff_divFamZarAffUniv
    81	      C hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 hO hchi i j hb)
    82	
    83	end Based
    84	
    85	include hO hchi in
    86	/-- The widened divisor functor has a representer in every genus.  The finite chart bases are
    87	chosen internally; genus zero is represented by the terminal object. -/
    88	noncomputable def divFunctorAffRepresenter :
    89	    Σ D : Over (Spec (.of k)), (divFunctorAff C g).RepresentableBy D := by
    90	  classical
    91	  by_cases hg : g = 0
    92	  · subst g
    93	    exact ⟨Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec (.of k))),
    94	      divFunctorAffZeroRepresentableBy (C := C) (pi := pi)⟩
    95	  · let r1 := Module.finrank k
    96	      ↥(divisorSections k (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤)
    97	    let r2 := Module.finrank k ↥(divisorSections k
    98	      ((windowM_choice pi hpi g + windowS_choice pi hpi g) • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤)
    99	    let b1 : Module.Basis (Fin r1) k
   100	        ↥(divisorSections k (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤) :=
   101	      Module.finBasis k _
   102	    let b2 : Module.Basis (Fin r2) k ↥(divisorSections k
   103	        ((windowM_choice pi hpi g + windowS_choice pi hpi g) • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤) :=
   104	      Module.finBasis k _
   105	    exact ⟨divSchemeOver k (windowS_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi)
   106	        (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) g r1 r2 b1
   107	        (b2.map (windowShiftEquiv hpi g).symm),
   108	      divFunctorAff_representableBy_divScheme_of_ne_zero
   109	        C hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 hg⟩
   110	
   111	/-- A chosen scheme representing the widened divisor functor. -/
   112	noncomputable def divRepAffScheme : Over (Spec (.of k)) :=
   113	  (divFunctorAffRepresenter C hpi g hO hchi).1
   114	
   115	/-- The widened divisor functor is represented by its chosen scheme, with no genus or chart-basis
   116	hypothesis. -/
   117	noncomputable def divFunctorAff_representableBy :
   118	    (divFunctorAff C g).RepresentableBy (divRepAffScheme C hpi g hO hchi) :=
   119	  (divFunctorAffRepresenter C hpi g hO hchi).2

   123	end AlgebraicGeometry

     9	/-!
    10	# The Jacobian challenge — statement file (with field base change)
    11	
    12	This is the single, self-contained **statement file** of the project: it collects every
    13	definition, instance, and theorem needed to *state* the main result, and nothing else. A reviewer
    14	reads this one file, compares it against the original challenge (`references/challenge.lean`, by
    15	Christian Merten) and its base-change extension, and is convinced the project formalizes the right
    16	thing. The genuinely-missing pieces are `sorry`; the base-change scaffolding (`baseChange`, the
    17	stability instances, `idIso`, `compIso`, and `Jacobian.congr` derived from `Jacobian.functor`) is
    18	genuinely proved here. Proofs of the `sorry`s live in the rest of the `AlgebraicJacobian/` tree and
    19	must not weaken or restate any signature below.
    20	
    21	By a **smooth curve** we mean a geometrically irreducible, smooth scheme of relative dimension one
    22	over a field, proper over that field.
    23	
    24	## Main definitions
    25	
    26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.genus` — genus of a proper, smooth curve.
    27	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian` — the Jacobian of a proper, smooth curve.
    28	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.ofCurve` — the Abel–Jacobi map associated to a `k`-rational point.
    29	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.functor` — functoriality of the Jacobian, bundled as a single
    30	  contravariant functor `(Curve k)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Grp (Over (Spec k))`.
    31	
    32	## Main theorems
    33	
    34	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus` — the Jacobian is smooth of relative
    35	  dimension `g = genus C`.
    36	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.exists_unique_ofCurve_comp` — the universal property: the Jacobian is
    37	  the Albanese variety of `C`.
    38	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.baseChangeIso` — the Jacobian commutes with base change of fields,
    39	  together with the identity/cocycle coherences (`baseChangeIso_id`, `baseChangeIso_comp`) and the
    40	  Abel–Jacobi compatibility `baseChange_ofCurve`.
    41	
    42	## Notes
    43	
    44	`noncomputable` is on the data-carrying declarations: their honest realizations rest on
    45	noncomputable Mathlib constructions. Names, argument types, and argument order are verbatim from
    46	the challenge; the `noncomputable` modifier is not a signature change.
    47	-/
    48	
    49	set_option autoImplicit false
    50	
    51	universe u
    52	
    53	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory MonObj
    54	
    55	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    56	
    57	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    58	  -- smooth curve
    59	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
    60	  -- proper
    61	  [IsProper C.hom]
    62	  -- geometrically irreducible
    63	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    64	
    65	/-- The category of smooth, proper, geometrically irreducible curves over `k`, with morphisms the
    66	morphisms of `k`-schemes. -/
    67	structure Curve (k : Type u) [Field k] where
    68	  /-- The underlying `k`-scheme. -/
    69	  carrier : Over (Spec (.of k))
    70	  [isProper : IsProper carrier.hom]
    71	  [smoothOfRelativeDimension : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 carrier.hom]
    72	  [geometricallyIrreducible : GeometricallyIrreducible carrier.hom]
    73	
    74	attribute [instance] Curve.isProper Curve.smoothOfRelativeDimension Curve.geometricallyIrreducible
    75	
    76	noncomputable instance (k : Type u) [Field k] : Category (Curve k) where
    77	  Hom X Y := X.carrier ⟶ Y.carrier
    78	  id X := 𝟙 X.carrier
    79	  comp f g := f ≫ g
    80	  id_comp := Category.id_comp
    81	  comp_id := Category.comp_id
    82	  assoc := Category.assoc
    83

    85	/-- The genus of a smooth proper curve: the `k`-dimension of the first cohomology group
    86	`H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` of the structure sheaf, viewed as a sheaf of `k`-modules on the small Zariski
    87	site of `C` (`Scheme.moduleKSheaf`), with cohomology the `Ext` from the constant sheaf
    88	(`CategoryTheory.Sheaf.HModule`). Finite-dimensionality of `H¹` is proved downstream. -/

    90	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] : ℕ :=
    91	  letI : C.left.Over (Spec (.of k)) := .ofHom C.hom

    97	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
    98	    Over (Spec (.of k)) :=

   112	instance smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus : SmoothOfRelativeDimension (genus C) (Jacobian C).hom :=

   114

   116	instance : IsProper (Jacobian C).hom :=
   117	  sorry
   118	
   119	/-- The Jacobian of `C` is geometrically irreducible over `k`. -/
   120	instance : GeometricallyIrreducible (Jacobian C).hom :=
   121	  sorry

   131	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   132	    (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) :

   134	  sorry

/bin/bash -lc 'set -euo pipefail
idx="$ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR/private-index-root-wrapper"
rm -f "$idx"
old=$("$HORIZON_GIT" rev-parse HEAD)
ref=$("$HORIZON_GIT" symbolic-ref HEAD)
GIT_INDEX_FILE="$idx" "$HORIZON_GIT" read-tree "$old"
GIT_INDEX_FILE="$idx" "$HORIZON_GIT" add -- AlgebraicJacobian.lean
GIT_INDEX_FILE="$idx" "$HORIZON_GIT" diff --cached --name-status "$old"
tree=$(GIT_INDEX_FILE="$idx" "$HORIZON_GIT" write-tree)
new=$(printf '"'%s\\n\\n%s\\n%s\\n%s\\n%s\\n%s\\n%s\\n'   'feat(divisors): root challenge-curve representer'   'Archon-Run: 0100'   'Archon-Session: 0012-horizon-pic-d'   'Archon-Role: horizon'   'Archon-Task: pic-d'   'Archon-Projects: Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild'   'Archon-Summary: Root the hypothesis-free genus-level widened divisor representer.' |   \""'$HORIZON_GIT" commit-tree "$tree" -p "$old")
"$HORIZON_GIT" update-ref "$ref" "$new" "$old"
"$HORIZON_GIT" diff-tree --no-commit-id --name-status -r "$old" "$new"
printf '"'%s\\n' \""'$new"'

      "body": "A \"TRAP, MEASURED -- DO NOT ROUTE VIA X\" NOTE IS THE HIGHEST-LEVERAGE FALSE CLAIM A LANE CAN SHIP, AND THE CHEAPEST TEST IS TO GREP WHETHER A SIBLING FILE ALREADY DOES X.\n\nWHAT HAPPENED (AJCR, pic-c 0092 r5, Pic0VanishingFieldGenusZero.lean:33-38). A lane recorded, in a file header, a commit message, and a direct message to another lane: \"going through chi_moduleKSheaf at baseChangeBundle C K produces the same object under a different Over instance, and the two chi terms DO NOT UNIFY -- measured\". It reads like exactly the kind of hard-won spelling fact worth broadcasting, and the receiving lane accepted it.\n\nIt is false. The bundled route closes with one `change` to the bundled spelling followed by `simpa`, at DEFAULT heartbeats. What had been measured was that one `simpa` failed without the `change`, i.e. a fact about a tactic invocation, published as a fact about two objects.\n\nTHE TEST THAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT COST ONE GREP. A sibling lane had written the prohibited proof, at a concrete curve, in the same hour, and it was at HEAD and root-imported: Curve/P1DegreeZeroTrivial.lean:83-99 uses chi_moduleKSheaf at baseChangeBundle with the same change + simpa. So before publishing \"route X does not work\", grep the tree for X: a live use site refutes the prohibition outright, and its presence in a file you did not write is more likely than it feels, because a prohibition is usually discovered exactly when two lanes are on the same object.\n\nWHY IT IS WORSE THAN AN ORDINARY OVERCLAIM. A positive overclaim gets tested when someone tries to use the result. A prohibition is never tested -- its whole function is to stop people trying -- so it can survive indefinitely and it forecloses a cheap route for every later round. Same asymmetry as [[gap-list-is-the-least-audited-prose]] and [[exculpatory-sentence-is-a-claim]], but with a longer half-life.\n\nCOROLLARY, same round, same file: unexplained `set_option maxHeartbeats 1600000` raises with a comment asserting the default is exceeded. Copying both files verbatim with the default budget: EXIT=0, all six declarations. A budget raise is a claim too, and re-running the file at the default is a 40-second check.",

      "body": "A THREE-LANE COMPOSITION IS INVISIBLE TO EVERY PER-ROW CHECK, AND THE ROWS WILL EACH TELL YOU THE WORK IS ELSEWHERE.\n\nWHAT HAPPENED (pic-e, AJC, 0095 r6). Three sorry-free theorems from three different lanes composed into a verbatim derivation of the project's central sorry from the classical pointed theorem: the unconditional finite-GALOIS-level rational point (Curve/), the picSharp->picEt transport (PicEtSubcanonical), and the lftFree descent step with hq and hcov already internal (PicEtGaloisQuotient). Eleven declarations, all axiom-clean, three commits.\n\nNO ROW MENTIONED THE OTHER TWO. The descent-assembly row listed FOUR open inputs; three were already discharged elsewhere. The seam docstring's own 'what remains' sentence listed three items, one of which was closed and one of which was DONE-AND-CALLED-REMAINING. Every row was individually plausible and internally consistent; the composition existed only across them.\n\nTHE MECHANISM, and why the usual checks miss it: each row is maintained by the lane that owns it, and a lane records what IT owes, not what another lane has since supplied. So a row goes stale in the CHEAP direction -- it schedules work that exists -- and nothing re-reads it, because a list of remaining obligations reads as self-criticism. Same asymmetry as [[gap-list-is-the-least-audited-prose]] and [[unavoidable-is-not-geometric]], but distributed: no single sentence is wrong enough to notice.\n\nTHE CHECK THAT FINDS IT, and it is cheap: take the consumer theorem's LITERAL binder list -- #check the one a costing tells you to aim at -- and ask of EACH binder, separately, 'does a producer for exactly this exist at HEAD?'. Not 'is this gap open' (the row answers that) but 'is this BINDER discharged'. At the spelling that matters, seamClauseOne_of_hasGaloisQuotient_lftFree, three of four were gone and the fourth was an instance binder no row named. A four-item gap list and a one-item binder list were both accurate about different things.\n\nCOROLLARY, the part that cost me a withdrawal: after composing, price the RESULT against the WEAKEST antecedent your proof consumes, not the shape the hand-off wants. My first antecedent carried IsSeparated, which is provably free from the conclusion's own representation, and a reduction whose antecedent contains a free conjunct misreports exactly the number it exists to report. Related: [[price-the-consumer-carrier]], [[audit-the-goals-antecedents-not-the-lemmas]].",

      "body": "VANISHING-VOCABULARY SPELLINGS ARE ONE ANTECEDENT -- and the commit that ships the 'reduced' producer often ships the iff that proves it is a re-spelling.\n\nAJC DivFamilyZero.lean, AJC.picrep.divzero, pic-e runs 0095->0105. Over three rounds the same lane landed three producers of Div0-representable, each 'reducing' the obligation to a fresh vocabulary:\n  _of_isZero               : IsZero x.F\n  _of_forall_subsingleton_sections : forall V, Subsingleton Gamma(x.F,V)\n  _of_forall_isEmpty_schematicSupport : IsEmpty(schematicSupport x.F)\nEach docstring bills its antecedent as 'the sharpest/purest/most-geometric honest form.' At every DivFamily x.F is quasicoherent, and the file itself ships isZero_iff_forall_subsingleton_sections and isZero_iff_isEmpty_schematicSupport -- so the three antecedents are PROVABLY EQUIVALENT (all = IsZero x.F). None is weaker. The obligation HasFiberDeg 0 -> IsZero x.F is untouched; only the vocabulary on its RHS rotates.\n\nTHE TELL, sharper than I-1622: when a 'reduction' commit also lands an IFF between the new antecedent and the old one, the iff IS the proof that no reduction happened. Emptiness-of-support, subsingleton-sections, and IsZero are one node with three names; a producer parameterised on any of them is the same producer. Before crediting 'reduced to X', rw the shipped iffs and check whether the new antecedent closes the old goal with no hypotheses -- if it does, it is coordinates, not distance. The real distance for divzero lives in DivSupportQuasiFinite.lean (carrier bridge + degree-0=>empty-fibre), which no spelling of the RHS moves.",

      "body": "DUPLICATION, DivisorFamilyDegreeZeroUnique.lean: the headline \"the FIRST inhabitant of DivFamZar at ANY parameter\" is FALSE over a field, and the uniqueness proof re-derives what two landed quotient-level lemmas already give.\n\nINHABITATION WAS NOT FIRST. exists_divFam_divFamDivisor_eq (DivisorFamilyFieldSurj.lean:143, the landed B-3 hsurj) at D = 0 gives a DivFam C K pi 0 with divFamDivisor = 0, hence DivFamZar C K pi 0 via toZar; divFamFieldEquiv.symm (0, le_rfl, by simp) gives the same class directly, and Quotient.out of it gives a CertifiedDivisorFamily C K pi 0. The correct claim is narrower and still worth having: trivZar is the first inhabitant at a GENERAL TEST RING R, where no field-surjectivity route applies.\n\nUNIQUENESS RE-DERIVES A LANDED LEMMA. presentationDivisor_eq_zero_of_isCertified_zero + divEq_of_isCertified_zero (:103, :114) work per-adaptation and then re-run divEq_of_presentationDivisor_eq. But divFamDivisor_injective (DivisorFamilyFieldEquiv.lean:177) is exactly that step already packaged at the QUOTIENT level, and DivisorFamilyDegreeZeroUnique.lean imports DivisorFamilyFieldEquiv directly. With zero_le_divFamDivisor (DivisorFamilyField.lean:165) and deg_divFamDivisor (DivisorFamilyFieldCRT.lean:376), both also in closure, the whole file's math is:\n  hx : divFamDivisor x = 0 := eq_zero_of_deg_le_zero K (zero_le_divFamDivisor x) (deg rewrite; norm_num)\n  same for y; exact divFamDivisor_injective (hx.trans hy.symm)\nVERIFIED at the file's exact import list minus DivisorFamilyDegreeZero, EXIT=0. Two of the three declarations in the \"Main declarations\" list are avoidable, and the docstring's \"in one line each\" argument describes the longer of two routes without noting the shorter one exists.\n\nALSO: instSubsingletonDivFamZarZero and uniqueZeroOfField carry [LocallyOfFiniteType (relCurve C K over Spec K)] which is NOT load-bearing: it is inferInstance from the SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 binder two lines up (Smooth => LocallyOfFiniteType).       "body": "REPLACING A HAND-ROLLED HYPOTHESIS BY 'THE STANDARD ONE' CAN STRENGTHEN IT INTO FALSITY -- and the test is a REFUTATION probe at the intended object, not a satisfiability witness.\n\nMEASURED (pic-e, AJC 0095 r7). I built the vocabulary the project was missing (graded prime avoidance => FiniteInAffine for projective schemes, all sorry-free), then restated the seam's antecedent with IsProjective of the representing scheme in place of the elementary FiniteInAffine, and committed 'entirely in standard vocabulary, no condition invented in this project'. I ran THREE vacuity checks and all three PASSED: the new conjunct is satisfiable (Spec k is projective over itself), it is NOT free (exact? fails at an arbitrary object), and the new antecedent does not close hypothesis-free. A fresh-context audit then refuted it in one step.\n\nWHY THE CHECKS MISSED IT. Every one of them asks 'could this hypothesis hold SOMEWHERE?'. None asks 'does it hold AT THE OBJECT THE STATEMENT IS ABOUT?'. IsProjective over a field forces IsProper, hence UniversallyClosed, hence CompactSpace over the compact Spec k -- and Pic_{C/k} is a disjoint union over deg in Z, so it is not quasi-compact. The antecedent is FALSE at its only intended witness. Satisfiability elsewhere is exactly what makes that invisible.\n\nWORSE: my own project already had the refutation. Picard/AmbientPicNotProper.lean exists to record this as 'trap (c): a P -> Q whose antecedent is unsatisfiable in the intended setting', with the general theorems to check it -- and I had imported nothing from it. The strengthening was FROM a weak condition my own file proved holds at the curve TO one my own project proved fails at the Picard scheme.\n\nTHE GENERALISABLE RULE. When you replace a hypothesis H by a 'more standard' H', H' => H is not enough -- that direction is what makes the substitution LOOK conservative. Ask what H' implies that H does not (here: quasi-compactness), then check that consequence at the intended witness. And grep your own tree for a file whose title is a negation ('NotProper', 'NoGo', 'Refute') before publishing a strengthening: the counterexample is often already landed one import away.\n\nALSO: the weakened repair is where tautologies hide. My first repair -- 'every finite set that lies in a good open lies in an affine open' -- is PROVABLE for every scheme with its hypothesis unused. Elaborate the candidate weakening with the binder discarded before shipping it (pic-g filed the same shape as I-1660 the same day).",
